text:
amy_sales: Quick sync — customer wants an on-prem air-gapped POC but they're nervous about upgrades/rollback windows. Can we outline a hardened rollback story they can show their infra team?

matt_eng: Absolutely. They usually ask for: signed artifacts, deterministic rollback steps, and a tested maintenance window that fits their business hours.

nora_se: Also add verification for artifact integrity (signatures + checksums) and a short TTL on keys. They specifically asked about running without outbound access.

amy_sales: They mentioned they run strict change freezes on last-week-of-quarter. Any way to offer emergency patching without breaking freeze policy?

sid_account: Pricing question from procurement: is emergency/after-hours support charged as a separate line item or rolled into Dedicated support?

ops_lead: We usually do: base Dedicated includes normal upgrades during agreed windows. After-hours emergency support is an add-on (SLA Premium) — we can quote as hourly or in a monthly retainer. Will confirm numbers with finance.

matt_eng: Back to rollback: recommended approach for air-gapped: deliver signed tarball of runtime + models + manifest. Provide a small verification utility (sha256 + GPG verify). Example:

```
sha256sum redwood-runtime-2026.03.1.tar.gz > redwood-runtime.sha256
gpg --verify redwood-runtime.tar.gz.sig redwood-runtime-2026.03.1.tar.gz
```

If verification fails, node should refuse install.

nora_se: We also require an offline certificate bundle and instructions to rotate it. For POC, a 30-day rotation policy is ok; production we'd recommend 90-day rotation with HSM integration.

amy_sales: They asked about delta patches instead of full installs to save time. Do we support signed deltas?

matt_eng: Yes — we produce delta archives for minor releases (patch-level). Deltas are signed the same way. For full major upgrades we recommend full image swap. Deltas are ~5–20% of full size depending on binary churn.

ops_lead: Rollback runbook (high level):
1) Stop inference service (graceful)
2) Ensure KV/cache is backed up: run `redwood-backup --local /tmp/backup`
3) Verify target artifact signature and checksum
4) Extract target artifact and run `redwood-install --rollback`
5) Run smoke tests and health checks (automated)
6) If smoke fails, re-run previous artifact from backup snapshot

Example command snippet we give customers:
```
# verify + install
gpg --verify release.sig release.tar.gz && sha256sum -c release.sha256 && tar xzf release.tar.gz -C /opt/redwood && /opt/redwood/bin/prepare && systemctl restart redwood
```

nora_se: Add to that: an automated pre-flight check that confirms model file compatibility (kv version, tokenizer hash). We don't want silent drift. Add a `--compat-check` to the install utility.

sid_account: Great — they also want a written SLA describing time-to-rollback support. Can we agree to a P0 rollback response within X hours for the POC?

ops_lead: For POC we can commit to 4-hour remote assistance during the maintenance window. For enterprise contracts we set tiers (1h/4h/24h).

amy_sales: Procurement will want that in the SOW. Also need clarity on upgrade cadence — they worry about cadence being 'too frequent'. What's reasonable?

matt_eng: Recommend: patch releases (security/hotfix) monthly, minor every 2–3 months, major ~biannual. For POC we can freeze on a pinned build and only deliver critical security patches as deltas.

nora_se: We'll include a security bulletin with each release and CVE notes. For air-gapped installs we provide a signed advisory bundle they can pull offline.

amy_sales: They asked about rollback testing — do we come onsite to run the first rollback?

ops_lead: We can offer an optional onsite eng day (paid) to validate the first install + rollback. Otherwise remote guidance + runbooks have worked in past POCs.

sid_account: Pricing follow-ups: please list the add-on line items: onsite eng day, after-hours premium SLA, yearly maintenance for signed delta hosting, license for private registry connector. I'll attach numbers later.

matt_eng: One operational constraint to flag — model weights >50GB currently require more careful transfer (pre-seed drives or encrypted disk shipping). For those we recommend a signed drive + shipping manifest process.

amy_sales: Nice. Anything about telemetry/privacy? Customer insists no outbound telemetry by default.

nora_se: Default is no telemetry. We provide an opt-in agent for metrics that can be toggled with a single flag. Audit logs are always local and included in the POC bundle.

deploy-bot: deploy job redwood/poc-image-verify/1765123457 completed — all artifacts signed and manifest uploaded to staging bucket (airgap-preview). :white_check_mark:

ops_lead: Action items:
- matt_eng to draft POC rollback runbook + compat-check commands (ETA: tomorrow)
- nora_se to prepare sample signed advisory + key rotation guide (ETA: 2 business days)
- sid_account & amy_sales to draft SOW lines for add-ons and maintenance pricing (ETA: EOD today)
- ops_lead to confirm emergency SLA tiers with finance (ETA: 48h)

amy_sales: I'll share this thread with the customer's infosec and ask for a follow-up sync. Thanks everyone :pray:

matt_eng: I'll add the --compat-check output to the smoke tests and include a small CI script.

nora_se: I'll include the GPG key fingerprints and recommended HSM integration notes in the advisory.

sid_account: Thanks — I'll loop in procurement and target a scoping call next week.

amy_sales: Closing notes: customer wanted assurance that rollback is single-command if preflight passes. We'll highlight that as an acceptance criterion in the POC doc.

ops_lead: +1. Keep us posted.
